description.ncbi_summary: This gene encodes a transcriptional regulator of sensory neuronal specification that plays a critical role in pain perception. The encoded protein contains an N-terminal PRDI-BF1 and RIZ homology (PR) domain, a SET domain, and three C-terminal C2H2 zinc finger DNA-binding domains. Naturally occurring mutations in this gene are associated with congenital insensitivity to pain (CIP), and hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies (HSAN's) affecting peripheral sensory and autonomic neurons. Deregulation of this gene is associated with solid cancers and hematological malignancies including chronic myeloid leukaemia. [provided by RefSeq, Mar 2017].

uniprot_function.text: Transcriptional regulator necessary for the development of nociceptive neurons, playing a key role in determining the nociceptive lineage from neural crest cell progenitors. Initiates neurogenesis and activates downstream pro-neuronal transcription factors, such as NEUROD1, BRN3A, and ISL1, specifically within nociceptive neurons, while repressing non-nociceptor cell fates. Essential for the proper function of nociceptors in adults, influencing both their excitability and their gene expression, thereby impacting how these neurons respond to various pain stimuli.
